title: the-ticket-inspector-speaks-the-spec-rule
intention: The ticket inspector's watchme_present check holds no opinion of its own about a complete WATCHME spec: it reports cairn/tools/base/watchme_spec.py's watchme_spec_error text, so a spec missing its receiver (or any field that module requires) is flagged at rest with the same words the cast door and the crossing use.
why: RULE 1 split of fa4a411c96be (2026-10-01): the inspector half of a-watchme-names-its-receiver lives in its own component. Lived symptom: the at-rest inspection and the cast door disagree about a complete WATCHME spec, so a receiver-less spec reads clean at rest.
traces_to: Law 1 and Law 4: one opinion about a complete spec, enforced where it is read. RULE 1: the inspector's change and its proof live in its own component.
how: In cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/inspector.py import watchme_spec_error from cairn.tools.base.watchme_spec (the tool's public function) beside the module's other imports, and replace the body of the 'if "WATCHME" in state:' block with: err = watchme_spec_error(t); if err: finding('watchme_present', err, {}). The 'none without because' check on a string watchme stays only if watchme_spec_error does not already report it (measure at build: run watchme_spec_error on {'workflow_and_state': <a WATCHME state>, 'watchme': 'none'}). In cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/proofs/test_inspector.py, test_watchme_with_spec_is_clean's spec gains receiver={'what': 'w', 'in': 'cairn/tools/base'}, and a new tooth test_watchme_present_carries_the_spec_rule_text asserts the finding text equals watchme_spec_error of a receiver-less fixture. Lands after fa4a411c96be is built (it adds the receiver rule this reports).
falsifier: RED if: (1) the ticket inspector's watchme_present finding on a fixture ticket at a WATCHME state whose spec lacks a receiver does not carry exactly watchme_spec_error's text for that ticket; (2) a fixture whose spec watchme_spec_error accepts yields a watchme_present finding; (3) cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/inspector.py still spells a WATCHME field name list of its own (grep for '"carrier"' in inspector.py finds a match). Horizon: the tester seal.
watchme: none, because the at-rest ticket inspection in cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/inspector.py is itself the receiver of the spec rule's text: every tick it reads every live ticket, and fa4a411c96be's W2 backfill consumes its watchme_present findings as its work list
children: none, because the change is one block in cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/inspector.py and its proof
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Where is the block? cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/inspector.py lines 159-181, '# --- WATCHME ---'. (2) What fixture state? 'code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> [BUILDME] -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(x) -> PROVED', the one test_watchme_present already uses. (3) Clause 3's tooth: assert '"carrier"' not in Path(inspector.py).read_text(). (4) PROVES = {ticket: {'1':..., '2':..., '3':...}}; the file already runs through print_teeth_main.

decisions.text: ORDER: this ticket crosses BUILDME only after fa4a411c96be's build commit has landed (watchme_spec_error must already require a receiver, or the text tooth has no receiver fault to compare). STEP 1, the red teeth in cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/proofs/test_inspector.py (it runs through print_teeth_main(__file__), which discovers every test_* function; no list to register in). (a) test_watchme_with_spec_is_clean (line 143): add receiver={'what': 'w', 'in': 'cairn/tools/base'} to its watchme dict. (b) New tooth test_watchme_present_carries_the_spec_rule_text: t = dict(CLEAN_TICKET, workflow_and_state='code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> [BUILDME] -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(x) -> PROVED', watchme={'object': 'x', 'trigger': 't', 'enough': 'e', 'carrier': 'c', 'nexus': 'n', 'consumer': 'u', 'probe': 'p'}); from cairn.tools.base.watchme_spec import watchme_spec_error inside the tooth; want = watchme_spec_error(t); assert want and 'receiver' in want; texts = [f['finding'] for f in inspect_ticket(t) if f['check'] == 'watchme_present']; assert texts == [want], texts. (Measure the finding dict's text key first: print one finding from test_watchme_present and use whatever key holds the message; the tooth must use that key.) (c) New tooth test_the_inspector_spells_no_watchme_field_list: src = (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'inspector.py').read_text(); assert '"carrier"' not in src. (d) PROVES = {'de9e31ef104c': {'1': 'test_watchme_present_carries_the_spec_rule_text', '2': 'test_watchme_with_spec_is_clean', '3': 'test_the_inspector_spells_no_watchme_field_list'}} at module level (merge into an existing PROVES dict if the file has one). Run red: (b) and (c) fail. Commit red.

STEP 2, the build in cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/inspector.py. Add from cairn.tools.base.watchme_spec import watchme_spec_error beside the module's other imports. Replace the body of the 'if "WATCHME" in state:' block (lines 160-181) with: err = watchme_spec_error(t) followed by if err: finding('watchme_present', err, {}). Before deleting the 'none without a because' branch, measure: watchme_spec_error({'workflow_and_state': 'code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> [BUILDME] -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(x) -> PROVED', 'watchme': 'none'}); if it returns None, keep that branch after the call (elif-free: a separate if over isinstance(wm, str)); if it returns a message, delete the branch. Run test_inspector.py green twice, then every cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/proofs/test_*.py; commit (pre-commit reseal in the background); seal with python3 -m cairn.devices.tester.cli --seal cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/proofs/test_inspector.py; commit.

Measured: cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/proofs/test_inspector.py line 23 defines CLEAN_TICKET = { ... } at module level, a dict fixture the existing teeth already build on with dict(CLEAN_TICKET, ...).

MEASURED 2026-10-01 at cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/inspector.py:77-83: inspect_ticket's finding() appends {ticket, check, finding, evidence}; the message text is under 'finding', structured data under 'evidence' (not 'details'). The teeth read f['check']=='watchme_present' and f['finding'] for the spec-rule sentence.
